senses: UK standard spelling of colorization.

Coagulated sour milk diluted with water.
Yoghurt (as used in Middle Eastern cuisine).
A fermented liquor made with coagulated sour milk.
A participant in the sport of fencing.
A person who makes, installs, repairs, or maintains fences.
A hand, as the part of the fore limb below the forearm in a human, or the corresponding part in other vertebrates.
ety: Borrowed from Latin manus (“hand”). Doublet of mano.

senses: Amateur film footage of a celebrity taken unofficially by a fan.
An edit which incorporates fancams.

EXID's Hani has made a splash with her fancam in 2014 and is now regarded as one of the hottest female idol stars.

senses: Characterised by or relating to typhus.
A talbotype.
ety: From Ancient Greek καλός (kalós, “good”) and τύπος (túpos, “impression”).
examples: Calotypes have a hazy and mysterious feeling about them and feel painterly in the way they look. Mastery of calotypes takes time. Every calotype is distinct and difficult to duplicate.

senses: Not wearing a bra.
Without a bra; not worn with a bra.
examples: To be more comfortable, her sister suggested to going to the store braless under her sweatshirt.

I find bras totally uncomfortable, hot and itchy, for both work and leisure. But looking around, I seem to be in the minority. What are the rules for going braless? Is it OK to show my nips, or is it rude?

senses: A specific theory concerning the lexicon.
ety: From Ancient Greek λεξικός (lexikós, “of words”), from λέξις (léxis, “a saying, speech, word”), from λέγειν (légein, “to speak”). By surface analysis, lexico- + -logy.

senses: A disposition for purposeful thinking and acting guided by criteria that are considered to be contextually appropriate and that are expected to result in positive outcomes related to the purpose.
In ancient catacombs and tombs of some types, a small separate chamber or recess cut into the rock, for the reception of a body or urn.
To excommunicate; curse.
ety: From Middle English mansien, apheretic variant of amansien, from Old English āmǣnsumian (“to excommunicate”). More at amanse.

senses: An old South American coin.
ety: Mid 19th century; via Spanish from Lokono kakabali.

senses: Of an empty environment that evokes a surreal blend of nostalgia, comfort, and unease; see liminal space.
ety: From Latin līmināris, from līmen (“doorstep, threshold; doorway, entrance; beginning, commencement”) + -ālis (suffix forming adjectives of relationship from nouns). Līmen is possibly derived from līmus (“askew; sideways”) (possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *Heh₃l- (“to bend, bow; elbow”)) + -men (suffix forming neuter nouns of the third declension) (from Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥ (suffix forming action nouns or result nouns from verbs)).

senses: A teahouse in Japan.
That tends to accumulate in an organism when the organism's ability to remove it is insufficient.
A fruit that has fallen to the ground rather than being picked; a windfall.
One of the large stones forming the base of a Cornish hedge.
ety: From Middle English grounder, grownder, equivalent to ground + -er.

senses: The meat or flesh of a pig, used especially for food; pork.
examples: A fire burned on the rock and fat dripped from the roasting pigmeat into the invisible flames.
The real purpose of this exorbitant barrel of pigmeat is to placate West Virginia politicians who complain their state doesn't get enough pork.

senses: One who, or that which, randomizes (often practically extended to pseudorandomization as well).
A video game mod that randomizes or shuffles gameplay elements, such as enemy spawning or loot, in order to make the game unpredictable or chaotic.
Prepared as a confection.
ety: From Late Latin cōnfectiōnārius (“one who prepares things by means of ingredients”), from Latin cōnfectiō (“preparing, producing”). See confection. By surface analysis, confection + -ary.
examples: Thy morning bounties ere I left my home, / The biscuit, or confectionary plum;

examples: They reached floor twenty-five. From this point onwards, thought Alex, a fall would be one hundred percent unsurvivable.

senses: One who complains, or is known for their complaints.
A complainant (an alleged victim in a criminal trial).
A body piercing consisting of an object positioned partially below and partially above the skin.
ety: From derm + -al. First attested in the early 19th century.
examples: Anchors with holes in the heel and toe of the foot are for dermals that are meant to be permanent. As the piercing heals, the tissue attaches to the foot around the holes, anchoring it in.

senses: A kind of Hindu-run village school.
One of two periods of cold and increased glaciation thousands of years before the present (Younger Dryas and Older Dryas).
ety: Borrowed from translingual Dryas for the plants, from both Latin Dryas and Ancient Greek Δρῠᾰ́ς (Drŭắs), derived from δρῦς (drûs, “tree, oak”). The second definition comes from the large quantity of pollen from the plant that is found in ice cores dating from these periods.

senses: A music genre from Cameroon, with a strong bass rhythm and prominent horn section.
Clothes to be worn in the daytime.
One who or that which resolves.
A device whose electrical output is proportional to the angular position of an object such as a rotor.
examples: On the Internet, a DNS resolver maps domain names to IP addresses.

senses: Having strings
ety: From Middle English strynged, y-strenged, equivalent to string + -ed.
examples: The violin is a stringed instrument but without frets.

senses: The steep artificial slope below a fort's parapet.
ety: Apheretic form of escarp. Doublet of escarp.

senses: A bus which is larger than or considered superior to ordinary buses.
Having, being, or relating to tubercles.
A human intertwined with electronic components; often implies the result is more electronic than biological.
ety: Blend of cybernetic + man, analyzable as cyber- + man. Originally a race of extraterrestrial enemies in the long-running British television series Doctor Who, first appearing in the 1966 serial The Tenth Planet.

senses: A person who plays games.
Achievement of sexual gratification by inflicting pain or humiliation on others, or watching pain or humiliation inflicted on others.
Deliberate or wanton cruelty, either mental or physical, to other people, or to animals, regardless of whether for (sexual) gratification.
